title: Lovász Local Lemma OQ-01: Assembling the Denominator Recursion (∏(1 − xⱼ) survival bound)
description: The denominator-step entry proved the single-neighbour peel (1 − x)·l ≤ μ[Aᶜ ∩ B | C] from l ≤ μ[B | C] and μ[A | B ∩ C] ≤ x — the transition that deflates a neighbour-survival lower bound by a factor (1 − x) when one more neighbour is avoided. Its docstring, and the OQ-01 knowledge base, flag the ITERATION of that peel — 'a well-founded recursion on |S₁|, still to be assembled' — as the missing mechanical core: the recursion producing the neighbour-block survival lower bound ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − xⱼ) ≤ μ[⋂_{j∈S₁} Aⱼᶜ | C] that the induction-step entry (cond_failure_le_x) consumes as its abstract denominator hypothesis d ≤ μ[⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ | C]. This entry lands that assembly. cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod is a Finset.induction on the neighbour block S: base S = ∅ gives ⋂_{j∈∅} Aⱼᶜ = univ, so μ[univ | C] = 1 (given μ C ≠ 0) matching the empty product; step insert k s (k ∉ s) factors the survival set as Aₖᶜ ∩ ⋂_{j∈s} Aⱼᶜ (set_biInter_insert) and the product as (1 − xₖ)·∏_s (prod_insert), and one application of the single peel mul_one_sub_le_cond_compl — fed the induction hypothesis ∏_s(1 − xⱼ) ≤ μ[⋂_s Aⱼᶜ | C] — extends the bound to insert k s. The two side conditions the peel needs at each step — positivity of every partial survival history μ[(⋂_T Aⱼᶜ) ∩ C] ≠ 0 and a per-event failure bound μ[Aₖ | (⋂_T Aⱼᶜ) ∩ C] ≤ xₖ — are carried as hypotheses quantified over ALL sub-blocks T ⊆ S, so the induction hypothesis has exactly the shape needed at every peel. The capstone cond_failure_le_x_prod threads the assembled product bound into the abstract induction-step invariant cond_failure_le_x, instantiating the previously-abstract denominator d with the concrete ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − xⱼ): under μ(Aᵢ) ≤ xᵢ·∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − xⱼ) it delivers μ[Aᵢ | (⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ) ∩ (⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ)] ≤ xᵢ — the shape the LLL strong induction threads. Honest scope: the recursion is mechanical GIVEN the per-event bounds; supplying those bounds is the mutually-recursive Erdős–Lovász invariant (this entry takes them as hypotheses, not axioms). 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

originalContributions: cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod: the denominator recursion — ∏_{j∈S} (1 − xⱼ) ≤ μ[⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ | C] for a finite neighbour block S, given that every partial survival history is non-null (μ[(⋂_{j∈T} Aⱼᶜ) ∩ C] ≠ 0 for T ⊆ S) and every per-event failure over a partial history is controlled (μ[Aₖ | (⋂_{j∈T} Aⱼᶜ) ∩ C] ≤ xₖ for k ∈ S, T ⊆ S, k ∉ T). This is the 'well-founded recursion on |S₁|, still to be assembled' flagged as the open mechanical core in the denominator-step docstring — assembled here by Finset.induction. Base S = ∅: ⋂_{j∈∅} Aⱼᶜ = univ, μ[univ | C] = 1 (cond_apply + ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel, μ C ≠ 0 from the empty-block positivity hypothesis) matching ∏_{∅} = 1. Step insert k s: set_biInter_insert and prod_insert factor both sides along the new neighbour, the side conditions restrict from insert k s down to s (feeding the induction hypothesis, since s ⊆ insert k s), and one application of mul_one_sub_le_cond_compl closes the step.

cond_failure_le_x_prod: the LLL induction-step invariant with the concrete ∏(1 − xⱼ) denominator. Threads cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod (with C = ⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ) into the abstract invariant cond_failure_le_x, instantiating the previously-abstract denominator d with the concrete neighbour product ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − xⱼ). Under the asymmetric LLL numeric hypothesis μ(Aᵢ) ≤ xᵢ·∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − xⱼ), the non-neighbour independence IndepSet (A i) (⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ) μ, and the per-sub-block side conditions the recursion consumes, it delivers μ[Aᵢ | (⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ) ∩ (⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ)] ≤ xᵢ — the exact shape the Lovász Local Lemma strong induction maintains at each conditioning event. This is the first OQ-01 result to state the induction invariant with the denominator NOT abstract but as the actual product the LLL recursion threads.

Framing contribution: closes the gap the induction-step entry left open. That entry proved the induction step closes 'once the denominator lower bound d is supplied'; the denominator-step entry proved the single peel that the recursion iterates. Neither assembled the iteration. This entry supplies exactly that Finset.induction, reducing the remaining open OQ-01 work to producing the per-event bounds xₖ from a dependency structure — the other half of the Erdős–Lovász mutual induction, for which cond_failure_le_x is the per-denominator engine.

overview.historicalContext: The Lovász Local Lemma (Erdős–Lovász, 1975) is proved by a strong induction maintaining the invariant Pr[Aᵢ | ⋂_{j∈S} Āⱼ] ≤ xᵢ for every subset S of the other events. Its induction step splits S = S₁ ⊔ S₂ into neighbours and non-neighbours of i and expands the conditional as a ratio Pr[Aᵢ | ⋂_S Āⱼ] = Pr[Aᵢ ∩ ⋂_{S₁} Āⱼ | ⋂_{S₂} Āⱼ] / Pr[⋂_{S₁} Āⱼ | ⋂_{S₂} Āⱼ]. The numerator is bounded above by Pr[Aᵢ] ≤ p; the denominator is bounded below by ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − xⱼ). That denominator bound is itself a recursion: peel the neighbours of i one at a time, each peel deflating the survival probability by a factor (1 − xₖ), where the per-peel factor is controlled by the SAME invariant at a strictly smaller conditioning set. This mutual recursion — the denominator product built from per-event bounds, the per-event bounds closed by the ratio using the denominator product — is the analytic heart of the Alon–Spencer presentation. The OQ-01 gallery front formalized the measure-theoretic surroundings: the two-block ratio identity and the closed ratio (induction-step entry), the numerator independence collapse (dependency-split entry), and the single-neighbour peel (denominator-step entry). What no entry had done is ITERATE the peel into the product ∏(1 − xⱼ). This entry supplies exactly that iteration, by Finset.induction over the neighbour block.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open question OQ-01 (from LovaszLocalLemma.lean)**: formalize the full probabilistic Lovász Local Lemma over measure-theoretic probability spaces, including the dependency-graph induction that produces per-event conditional bounds from a bounded dependency degree.

**This entry (the denominator recursion)**: assemble, by well-founded recursion on the neighbour block S₁, the survival lower bound ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − xⱼ) ≤ μ[⋂_{j∈S₁} Aⱼᶜ | C] from the single-neighbour peel — given per-event failure bounds μ[Aₖ | (⋂_T Aⱼᶜ) ∩ C] ≤ xₖ and positivity of every partial history over the sub-blocks T ⊆ S₁ — and thread it into the abstract induction-step invariant cond_failure_le_x to obtain μ[Aᵢ | (⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ) ∩ (⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ)] ≤ xᵢ with the denominator instantiated to the concrete product.
overview.text: The Lovász Local Lemma keeps one number under control through an induction — the chance a bad event happens given some others are avoided. The hard half of each step is a lower bound on how likely a block of 'neighbour' events all avoid firing, given the rest survive. An earlier entry proved the single move: adding one more avoided neighbour shrinks that survival probability by at most a factor (1 − xₖ). But one move is not the bound; you have to iterate it across all the neighbours to get a PRODUCT ∏(1 − xⱼ). This entry does the iteration — a clean induction over the block of neighbours, peeling one at a time, each peel feeding the running product. It then plugs the assembled product into the ratio machinery a sibling entry built, turning the abstract 'some denominator bound' into the concrete ∏(1 − xⱼ) the textbook proof actually uses. The honest catch: each peel needs a per-event bound, and those bounds are exactly what the ratio machinery PRODUCES — the two halves are mutually recursive. This entry supplies the denominator half of that mutual recursion, taking the per-event bounds as explicit inputs.
overview.proofStrategy:
**The recursion (cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod).** Finset.induction on the neighbour block S, with the side conditions (positivity of every partial history, per-event bound over every partial history) quantified over sub-blocks T ⊆ S so the induction hypothesis carries them. Base S = ∅: ⋂_{j∈∅} Aⱼᶜ = univ (simp), so the goal is 1 ≤ μ[univ | C]; cond_apply hC unfolds μ[univ | C] = (μ C)⁻¹·μ(C ∩ univ), Set.inter_univ and ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel (μ C ≠ 0 from the empty-block positivity hypothesis, μ C ≠ ∞ from measure_ne_top) reduce it to 1, matching Finset.prod_empty = 1. Step insert a s (a ∉ s): restrict hpos/hbound from insert a s down to s via s ⊆ insert a s (Finset.subset_insert) and feed the induction hypothesis IH : ∏_s(1 − xⱼ) ≤ μ[⋂_s Aⱼᶜ | C]; Finset.prod_insert factors the product as (1 − xₐ)·∏_s and Finset.set_biInter_insert factors the survival set as (A a)ᶜ ∩ ⋂_s Aⱼᶜ; then mul_one_sub_le_cond_compl (hA a) (Finset.measurableSet_biInter for ⋂_s Aⱼᶜ) hC (positivity hpos s) (per-event bound hbound a) IH closes the goal to exactly (1 − xₐ)·∏_s ≤ μ[(A a)ᶜ ∩ ⋂_s Aⱼᶜ | C].

**The capstone (cond_failure_le_x_prod).** Set C = ⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ (measurable via Finset.measurableSet_biInter); cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod supplies hden : ∏_{S₁}(1 − xⱼ) ≤ μ[⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ | ⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ]; then cond_failure_le_x hA S₁ S₂ i hposC hNC hindep hden hprod0 hlll instantiates the abstract denominator d := ∏_{S₁}(1 − xⱼ) and closes to μ[Aᵢ | (⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ) ∩ (⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ)] ≤ xᵢ.
keyInsights: The peel was proved; only the iteration was missing. The denominator-step entry proved (1 − x)·l ≤ μ[Aᶜ ∩ B | C] — one neighbour peeled — and explicitly deferred 'a well-founded recursion on |S₁|, still to be assembled'. That recursion is a plain Finset.induction: each insert step is one peel, and Aᵢᶜ ∩ ⋂_{s} Aⱼᶜ = ⋂_{insert a s} Aⱼᶜ (set_biInter_insert) is precisely why one peel advances the block by one element. Naming the induction and threading the side conditions is the whole content.

Carrying the side conditions over ALL sub-blocks is what makes the induction go through. The peel at step 'insert a s' needs the per-event bound and positivity at the partial history ⋂_s Aⱼᶜ — a strictly smaller block. Quantifying both hypotheses over every T ⊆ S (rather than only S itself) lets the induction hypothesis at s inherit exactly the bounds it needs, since s ⊆ insert a s restricts the quantifier cleanly. This is the finitary shadow of the strong induction 'at strictly smaller conditioning sets' in the textbook proof.

The empty block is the independence collapse in disguise. Base case S₁ = ∅ gives the empty product 1 and μ[univ | C] = 1: with no neighbours, the survival lower bound is trivially 1, and the induction step reduces (via cond_failure_le_x_prod) to μ[Aᵢ | C] = μ(Aᵢ) ≤ xᵢ — the pure non-neighbour independence collapse already proved in the dependency-split and base-case entries. The recursion interpolates between that collapse and the full neighbour product.

This closes the denominator half of the Erdős–Lovász mutual induction. cond_failure_le_x_prod now states the maintained invariant μ[Aᵢ | history] ≤ xᵢ with the denominator NOT abstract but equal to the concrete ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − xⱼ). The only remaining open piece is supplying the per-event bounds xₖ from a measure-theoretic dependency structure — and cond_failure_le_x (which this entry consumes) is exactly the engine that produces one such bound per denominator, so the two directions of the mutual recursion are now both formalized; wiring them into a single unconditional LLL is the final OQ-01 target.

Arbitrary neighbour block, not a prefix — that is why the peel is iterated rather than transported. The sibling conditional-avoidance entry proves a product survival bound ∏(1 − bₖ) ≤ μ[⋂ᵢ Aᵢᶜ | H] over PREFIX histories, where a change-of-measure transport suffices because each new event conditions on a nested initial segment. Here the block S₁ is an arbitrary Finset ℕ of neighbours with no order structure, so no prefix transport applies; the bound must be built element-by-element by Finset.induction, each insertion peeling one neighbour via mul_one_sub_le_cond_compl. This is the version the dependency-graph induction genuinely needs, since a vertex's neighbourhood in the dependency graph is an unordered set, not an initial segment.
prerequisites: The single-neighbour survival peel mul_one_sub_le_cond_compl : (1 − x)·l ≤ μ[Aᶜ ∩ B | C], and conditional finiteness cond_ne_top, from lovasz-local-lemma-oq-01-denominator-step
The abstract induction-step invariant cond_failure_le_x : μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·d ⇒ μ[Aᵢ | N ∩ C] ≤ x, from lovasz-local-lemma-oq-01-induction-step
ProbabilityTheory.cond and IndepSet over an IsProbabilityMeasure; ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel, cond_apply

conclusion.summary: The denominator recursion of the Erdős–Lovász induction is machine-verified over an arbitrary probability space: ∏_{j∈S}(1 − xⱼ) ≤ μ[⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ | C] by Finset.induction iterating the single-neighbour survival peel (cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod), and its threading into the abstract induction-step invariant to give μ[Aᵢ | (⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ) ∩ (⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ)] ≤ xᵢ with the denominator instantiated to the concrete product ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − xⱼ) (cond_failure_le_x_prod). 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications:
**Assembles the iteration the denominator-step entry deferred.** That entry proved one neighbour peel and explicitly left 'a well-founded recursion on |S₁|, still to be assembled'; this entry supplies that recursion as a plain Finset.induction, and the induction-step entry's abstract invariant now specialises, via cond_failure_le_x_prod, to the concrete ∏(1 − xⱼ) denominator the textbook LLL uses.

**Honest scope**: this is the denominator half of the Erdős–Lovász mutual induction, not the full LLL. The per-event failure bounds μ[Aₖ | (⋂_T Aⱼᶜ) ∩ C] ≤ xₖ over partial sub-histories are explicit hypotheses; producing them from a measure-theoretic dependency structure is the other half of the mutual recursion (cond_failure_le_x is its per-denominator engine). Wiring the two directions into a single unconditional LLL — a joint well-founded induction on |S| threading both the denominator product and the per-event bounds — remains the open OQ-01 target. This entry supplies the previously-missing denominator recursion both directions require.
openQuestions: Close the Erdős–Lovász mutual recursion: combine cond_failure_le_x_prod (denominator half, this entry) with the per-event-bound half (cond_failure_le_x as the per-denominator engine) into a single well-founded induction on |S| that discharges the hpos/hbound side conditions internally instead of taking them as hypotheses — yielding the unconditional invariant μ[Aᵢ | ⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ] ≤ xᵢ for every finite S. This is the open OQ-01 target.

Derive the per-event failure bounds μ[Aₖ | (⋂_T Aⱼᶜ) ∩ C] ≤ xₖ from a measure-theoretic dependency structure (a symmetric or directed dependency graph with IndepSet Aᵢ against non-neighbour intersections), rather than assuming them, so the recursion's inputs are produced from a bounded dependency degree as in the classical LLL hypothesis.

Discharge the partial-history positivity hypotheses (μ[(⋂_T Aⱼᶜ) ∩ C] ≠ 0 for all T ⊆ S) from the numeric LLL budget itself: in the classical statement the bounds xⱼ ∈ (0,1) with μ(Aⱼ) ≤ xⱼ∏(1 − xₖ) already force every partial survival history to be strictly positive, so the positivity side conditions should be derivable, not assumed.

Extract the quantitative conclusion μ(⋂ᵢ Aᵢᶜ) ≥ ∏ᵢ(1 − xᵢ) > 0 (probability that NO bad event occurs) by iterating cond_failure_le_x_prod over the full index set, recovering the usable existence form of the LLL from the maintained conditional invariant.

Generalise from finite neighbour blocks to a countably infinite dependency graph with locally finite neighbourhoods, checking that the Finset.induction over each finite neighbourhood composes into the countable product ∏(1 − xⱼ) under the appropriate ENNReal tprod / limit.

crossReferences.description: Supplies the single-neighbour survival peel mul_one_sub_le_cond_compl : (1 − x)·l ≤ μ[Aᶜ ∩ B | C], the engine this entry iterates. The denominator-step docstring explicitly defers 'a well-founded recursion on |S₁|, still to be assembled' — cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod is that recursion.

Supplies the abstract induction-step invariant cond_failure_le_x, which takes the denominator lower bound d ≤ μ[N | C] as a hypothesis. The capstone cond_failure_le_x_prod threads this entry's assembled product ∏(1 − xⱼ) into it, instantiating the previously-abstract d with the concrete neighbour product — the shape the induction-step entry flagged as its remaining open core.

Provides the non-neighbour independence collapse μ[Aᵢ | ⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ] = μ(Aᵢ), which is the empty-neighbour-block (S₁ = ∅) special case of the invariant cond_failure_le_x_prod closes here: no neighbours ⇒ empty product 1 ⇒ μ[Aᵢ | C] = μ(Aᵢ) ≤ xᵢ.

Proves the product-form denominator lower bound ∏(1 − bₖ) ≤ μ[⋂ᵢ Aᵢᶜ | H] over PREFIX histories by transport of measure. cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod proves the analogous product bound over an ARBITRARY finite neighbour block (not a prefix), by iterating the conditional-probability peel rather than transporting measure — the version the dependency-graph induction genuinely needs.

The d = 0 base case μ(⋂ Aᵢᶜ) = ∏(1 − μ(Aᵢ)) from full mutual independence. The denominator recursion here generalises the product structure of that identity to conditional survival over an arbitrary neighbour block, replacing exact independence by the per-event failure bounds of the dependency graph.
